'''''Sabal minor''''', commonly known as the '''dwarf palmetto''',<ref>{{PLANTS |id=SAMI8 |taxon=''Sabal minor'' |accessdate=26 October 2015 }}</ref> is a small species of [[Arecaceae|palm]]. It is native to the deep southeastern and south-central [[United States]] and northeastern [[Mexico]]. It is naturally found in a diversity of habitats, including maritime forests, swamps, floodplains, and occasionally on drier sites.<ref name=fna/> It is often found growing in [[calcareous]] [[marl]] soil.<ref name=Weakley>{{cite web |url=http://www.herbarium.unc.edu/flora.htm |title= Flora of the Southern and Mid-Atlantic States by Alan Weakley}}</ref> ''Sabal minor'' is one of the most frost and cold tolerant among [[North America]]n palms.

==Distribution==
This palm's native range spans on the Atlantic Coast from central [[Florida]] north to at least [[Monkey Island, North Carolina]],<ref name=Weakley/> possibly also extreme southeastern [[Virginia]].<ref>https://www.pubs.ext.vt.edu/HORT/HORT-60/HORT-60.html</ref><ref>https://fsus.ncbg.unc.edu/cust/2024/main.php?pg=show-taxon-detail.php&taxonid=991</ref> On the Gulf Coast, it spans from central Florida to central [[Texas]], [[Arkansas]], north to southern [[Oklahoma]] and northern [[Alabama]] in the [[Great Appalachian Valley|Coosa Valley]], then south in the State of [[Nuevo León]] in [[Mexico]].<ref name=e>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=181048 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref>

==Description==
''Sabal minor'' grows up to {{convert|3|m|sp=us}} in height, with a trunk up to {{convert|30|cm|sp=us}} diameter. It is a [[List of Arecaceae genera#Tribe Corypheae|fan palm]] (Arecaceae tribe Corypheae), with the [[leaf|leaves]] with a bare petiole terminating in a rounded fan of numerous leaflets. Each leaf is {{convert|1.5|-|2|m|abbr=on}} long, with 40 leaflets up to {{convert|80|cm|abbr=on}} long, conjoined over half of this length. The [[flower]]s are yellowish-white, {{convert|5|mm|sp=us}} across, produced in large compound [[panicle]]s up to {{convert|2|m|abbr=on}} long, extending out beyond the leaves. The [[fruit]] is a black [[drupe]] {{convert|1|to|1.3|cm|in|1|abbr=on}} long containing a single seed.<ref name=fna>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=200027117 ''Sabal minor''] in Flora of North America</ref>

While usually being small and shrubby, ''Sabal minor'' can become tree-like as it ages.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center - The University of Texas at Austin |url=https://www.wildflower.org/plants/result.php?id_plant=sami8 |access-date=2025-09-11 |website=www.wildflower.org}}</ref> 

==Cultivation==
''Sabal minor'' is one of the most cold hardy palms in cultivation; however, it does best when grown in [[continental climate]]s with hot and humid tropical summer conditions, and may struggle or grow slowly in cool summer [[oceanic climate]]s. It is hardy to around {{convert|-15|C}},<ref>{{cite web | title=Sabal: how to plant, grow, and care for it? | website=Irish blog Promesse de fleurs | date=2021-08-24 | url=https://www.promessedefleurs.ie/gardening-tips/familysheet/sabal-planting-growing-and-maintaining/ | access-date=2025-12-19}}</ref> with selected [[cultivar]]s hardy to {{convert|-20|C}} when established.<ref>{{cite web | title=Palm Grower's Guide | website=Palmpedia | date=2010-01-29 | url=https://www.palmpedia.net/wiki/Sabal_minor | access-date=2025-12-19}}</ref> It is generally cultivated in subtropical and warm temperate climates. ''S.{{nbsp}}minor'' can grow in a wide variety of soil types, and is often found submerged in swamps in the [[southeastern United States]]. It grows in both full sun and shaded locations, though it will do best in the cooler garden zones (below [[Hardiness zone|USDA Zone 7]]) in full sun and a wind-sheltered location. 

In the United States, since the 1960s, cultivation of ''Sabal minor'' has spread beyond the deep southern United States. ''S.{{nbsp}}minor'' is cultivated along the East Coast from [[Florida]] to [[Connecticut]], and on the West Coast from [[Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada|Vancouver]] BC south to [[San Diego]]. It is a recommended horticultural plant by the [[Virginia Cooperative Extension]].<ref>[https://www.pubs.ext.vt.edu/HORT/HORT-60/HORT-60-PDF.pdf ''Care Sheet for ''Sabal minor'' or "Dwarf Palmetto" in Virginia Landscapes Fact and Care Sheet for Virginia Gardens'']</ref> There are several cultivars, including those from the [[Outer Banks|Outer Banks of North Carolina]] (northernmost strains), and those from [[Oklahoma]] and [[Texas]]. One popular strain is 'McCurtain', named after [[McCurtain County, Oklahoma]], where they are native. These tend to remain trunkless and smaller than those from warmer areas. ''S.{{nbsp}}minor'' is a popular landscape palm in coastal resort areas from [[Virginia Beach]], Virginia, to southern Texas.
